name: Ansible
description: Protects against destructive Ansible operations like dangerous shell \ commands and unchecked playbook runs

destructive_patterns.name: shell-rm-rf
destructive_patterns.description: Ansible shell/command with 'rm -rf' is destructive. Review carefully.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Running 'rm -rf' via Ansible shell or command module executes destructive deletion \ across all targeted hosts simultaneously. This multiplies the impact compared to \ running it locally:

\ - Files deleted on every host in inventory or pattern \ - No confirmation or dry-run by default \ - Parallel execution means rapid, widespread destruction \ - Cannot be undone without backups on each host

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use file module with state=absent for managed deletion \ - Add --check flag to preview which hosts would be affected \ - Use --limit to restrict to specific hosts first \ - Verify target path with debug module before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: shell-reboot
destructive_patterns.description: Ansible shell/command with reboot/shutdown affects system availability.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Rebooting or shutting down systems via Ansible affects all targeted hosts at once. \ This can cause service outages across your infrastructure:

\ - All services on affected hosts become unavailable \ - No graceful draining of connections or traffic \ - Database transactions may be interrupted \ - Load balancer health checks will fail

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use the reboot module which handles wait_for_connection \ - Add serial: 1 to playbook for rolling reboots \ - Use --limit to test on single host first \ - Coordinate with maintenance windows

destructive_patterns.name: playbook-all-hosts
destructive_patterns.description: ansible-playbook without --check or --limit may affect all hosts. Use --check first.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Running ansible-playbook without --check or --limit applies changes to all hosts in \ the inventory. This is risky for destructive playbooks:

\ - Every host matching the play's pattern is affected \ - Mistakes propagate to entire infrastructure at once \ - No opportunity to verify changes before they're applied \ - Rollback may be difficult or impossible

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Add --check --diff to preview changes \ - Use --limit host1,host2 to test on subset \ - Add serial: 1 to playbook for rolling updates \ - Review the playbook tasks before running

destructive_patterns.name: extra-vars-delete
destructive_patterns.description: Ansible extra-vars contains potentially destructive keywords. Review carefully.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Extra variables containing destructive keywords like 'delete', 'remove', 'destroy', \ or 'drop' may trigger conditional destructive actions in playbooks:

\ - Variables may control whether resources are deleted \ - Typos in variable values could trigger unintended paths \ - Variable precedence may override safer defaults

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review playbook to understand how variables are used \ - Add --check to see what tasks would run \ - Use --limit to test on single host first \ - Consider using vault-encrypted vars for destructive flags
